title: Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE)
summary: Generate a hypothetical relevant passage to improve retrieval alignment, then answer only from real retrieved evidence.
overview: Hypothetical Document Embeddings, or HyDE, addresses the mismatch between a short query and the longer documents indexed by a dense retriever. A language model creates a plausible answer-like passage; an encoder embeds that hypothetical passage and uses it to search the real corpus. The generated text is a retrieval aid, not a factual source.

HyDE can help when a query lacks the vocabulary or structure found in relevant documents. It can also steer retrieval toward a fabricated assumption, especially for rare entities or ambiguous questions. Retaining the original query and comparing direct retrieval provides a useful control, while fusion can reduce dependence on one hypothetical generation.

production.poc: A prototype compares direct-query embeddings with HyDE on zero-shot retrieval examples and labels topic drift.
production.production: Production constrains generation, excludes invented details from the final evidence set, and caps added model latency.
production.scale: At scale, evaluate benefits by query class, cache safe hypothetical representations, and version the generator and embedding model together.

components.name: Hypothetical passage generator
components.role: Produces domain-shaped search text while preserving known query constraints.

components.name: Embedding encoder
components.role: Maps the generated passage into the same space as real documents.

components.name: Real document index
components.role: Returns actual source passages with provenance and authorization metadata.

components.name: Fusion controller
components.role: Optionally combines HyDE and direct-query candidates.

components.name: Evidence-only answer stage
components.role: Uses retrieved sources and excludes the hypothetical passage as authority.

flow.title: Assess suitability
flow.description: Choose HyDE when vocabulary mismatch is plausible and direct retrieval may be weak.

flow.title: Generate search text
flow.description: Create a bounded hypothetical passage that retains explicit entities and constraints.

flow.title: Embed the hypothesis
flow.description: Encode the passage with the corpus-compatible model.

flow.title: Retrieve real evidence
flow.description: Search the authorized corpus and optionally combine direct-query results.

flow.title: Validate alignment
flow.description: Reject candidates driven by unsupported hypothetical details or changed intent.

flow.title: Answer from sources
flow.description: Generate a cited answer from real passages, or abstain if evidence remains absent.

useCase.title: Finding an unfamiliar failure mechanism
useCase.situation: An engineering assistant searches a technical library for descriptions of a surface defect expressed in informal language.
useCase.problem: The user’s short description shares few terms with the relevant materials reports.
useCase.requirement: Improve retrieval vocabulary without asserting a diagnosis from generated text.
useCase.architecture: HyDE generates a candidate technical description and combines its retrieved passages with direct-query results.
runtime: The hypothetical passage introduces likely descriptive terminology.
The answer stage compares real reports and states only mechanisms supported by those sources.
useCase.failure: If the hypothetical text invents an alloy or operating condition, constraint validation rejects that retrieval branch.
useCase.impact: Measure recall improvement, hypothetical drift, and added latency; success means finding better real evidence, not producing a convincing invented document.

tradeoffs.cost: Adds generation cost and assumption risk.
Multiply retrieval work and need deduplication.

tradeoffs.benefit: Preserves a baseline independent of generated details.

failures.detection: Retrieved passages reflect an invented diagnosis.
failures.recovery: Compare original constraints and diversify or discard the hypothesis.

failures.detection: The final response cites content absent from the corpus.
failures.recovery: Keep hypothetical text outside the evidence schema.

mistakes.fix: Use it only to locate real evidence.
Preserve unknowns and validate explicit constraints.
Enable it only on evaluated query classes.

whenToUse: Use for short descriptive queries with vocabulary mismatch.
Use for zero-shot retrieval where relevance labels are scarce.
Use when added latency yields measured recall gains.
whenNotToUse: Avoid exact identifier lookups already handled lexically.
Do not use hypotheses as factual evidence.
Avoid ambiguous high-impact questions without alignment checks.
checklist: Evaluate against direct retrieval on the same questions.
